sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Pipeline DAG Order and Leakage Audit Studio! Toggle the scope selector between global pre-CV fitting and encapsulated Pipeline isolation to see how fold boundaries govern cross-validation honesty versus out-of-sample collapse.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, switching from Certified Encapsulated Pipeline to Global SelectKBest shoots our cross-validation AUC to 0.921 while production crashes to 0.502! That proves mutual information leakage creates fake validation certainty, Kaito! Keep every estimator and selector sealed inside CV folds.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Missingness Nullity Matrix and Correlation Inspector! Switch between independent MCAR drops, positive joint panel batteries, and mutually exclusive branching to observe Pearson phi correlation coefficients live.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, look at the barcode matrix! In Joint Panel Battery mode, nulls align horizontally with phi above +0.85, whereas branching creates a negative alternating pattern! Visual nullity telemetry instantly exposes hidden missingness mechanisms before imputation, Kaito.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Active Checkpoint 1. Diagnose why running SelectKBest globally across 100 random Gaussian noise rows and 1,000 features prior to cross-validation yields an illusory 0.92 ROC-AUC.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, if all 1,000 columns are completely random noise, how does SelectKBest find 15 columns that score 0.92 in cross-validation? Because across 1,000 trials, random noise creates spurious matches with the target labels—and peeking at validation labels before splitting lets the selector cherry-pick columns tuned to the test fold, Kaito!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Active Checkpoint 2. Interpret why nullity correlation yields plus 0.92 between Income and Credit Score, versus minus 0.88 between Employment Years and Retirement Years.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, why should we treat +0.92 completely differently from -0.88 in the same dataset? Because +0.92 means two sensors or APIs failed together, Kaito—whereas -0.88 indicates mutually exclusive form skip-logic where missing simply means Not Applicable and must never be mean-imputed!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! Across 1,000 random noise columns, chance alone creates spurious alignments with y. Running SelectKBest globally peeks at validation fold labels before splitting, leaking test target knowledge into feature masks. Pipeline encapsulation eliminates this mirage.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite. Logistic Regression is not memorizing row indices. The leak occurs because fitting SelectKBest over all rows globally examines validation labels y_val ahead of splitting, cherry-picking columns that spuriously match the test fold.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Positive +0.92 reflects concurrent MAR bureau or API outages requiring conditional multivariate imputation or missingness flags, while negative -0.88 signals skip-logic form branching where missing means Structurally Not Applicable.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! A negative correlation of minus 0.88 does not mean MCAR noise or require dropping rows. It signals mutually exclusive conditional branching where one answered field logically precludes the other—never overwrite Not Applicable entries with global means.
